postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — the `raw_html` cook path returns `raw` verbatim as `cooked`, storing and rendering remote HTML (RSS `content`, Readability output) unsanitized, enabling stored XSS from a compromised or hostile feed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` and `PollFeed`/`import_remote` create posts from remote RSS/Readability HTML and set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. RSS content is only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (scrub is encoding cleanup, not HTML sanitization), so hostile/compromised feed HTML (e.g., script tags or dangerous attributes) would be stored and rendered verbatim, enabling stored XSS. Readability whitelists some tags/attributes, but RSS import does not, making the issue directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — the Readability path whitelists `href`, permitting `javascript:` URLs

adjudication.rationale: The diff change at app/models/post.rb adds a `cook_method` enum and a bypass that returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, but it does not contain any Readability-related whitelisting logic. The only Readability usage/whitelist in this diff is in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` (`Readability::Document.new(... attributes: %w[href src])`). So the finding’s cited location (`post.rb:131`) is incorrect, and the specific claim that this “permits `javascript:` URLs” depends on ruby-readability’s internal sanitization behavior, which is not shown in the diff and thus is not directly verifiable from it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — the feed-supplied `url` is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`, so a link containing a single quote injects arbitrary attributes/markup

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")` directly into `contents` without escaping. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still allows quotes and other characters after the scheme (e.g. `http://example.com/' onmouseover='...`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw`, this HTML is ultimately rendered via `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, so a crafted URL can inject arbitrary attributes/markup (XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — check-then-insert against the unique `embed_url` index is racy: two concurrent `RetrieveTopic` jobs (or a job racing the scheduled poll) both see `embed.blank?` and the second raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`; the redis throttle doesn't cover it because `no_throttle` is set for staff

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import` the code does a non-atomic check-then-insert: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` when `embed.blank?`. There is a unique DB index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), but no locking or retry around the create, so two concurrent callers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then the second `create!` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (and may also create an extra topic/post before failing). This race is plausible because `RetrieveTopic` can run concurrently for the same `embed_url` (the redis throttle is bypassed when `no_throttle` is set, e.g., staff) and `TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve` / `PollFeed` can also invoke imports concurrently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — `embed.post` is nil when the post was deleted/trashed, so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises on the next feed update; the surviving `TopicEmbed` row also permanently blocks re-import and makes `topic_id_for_embed` point at a deleted topic

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed row is found (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`), the code unconditionally does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, runs `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)`. There is no guard for `embed.post` being `nil` (e.g., if the referenced Post is deleted or otherwise not returned by the association). In that case `PostRevisor` will be initialized with `nil` and will raise when it tries to access `@post` during revision. Additionally, the existence of the `topic_embeds` row (unique `embed_url` index, and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` bailing out if any row exists) will prevent recreating the topic/post, and `topic_id_for_embed` will continue to return the stored `topic_id` even if that topic/post no longer exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:62,69 — protocol-relative URLs starting with `//` are rewritten as absolute paths (e.g. `//cdn.example.com/x.png` becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`), breaking every protocol-relative link and image in imported content

adjudication.rationale: Real issue in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`: it rewrites any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png` also start with `/`, so the code strips all leading slashes via `sub(/^\/+/, '')` and then prepends `prefix` (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com/`), producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which breaks protocol-relative links/images. This behavior is directly present in the diff and will affect imported content passed through `absolutize_urls`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — adding `force: true` to an already-committed migration turns any re-run into a silent `DROP TABLE top_topics`, destroying existing rows; the local DB state should be fixed instead of editing a shipped migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. Since this is an edit to a previously existing migration file, any scenario where that migration is executed while `top_topics` already exists (e.g., a redo/manual rerun, or a new environment that already has the table from prior state) would silently drop existing rows. This risk is directly introduced by the diff and is not just a style concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` on `posts` takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and rewrites the whole table on PostgreSQL < 11, causing a multi-minute outage on a large forum

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null DEFAULT causes a full table rewrite and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, which can be a serious outage risk on a large `posts` table. This is a real operational defect introduced by the migration as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously downloads and imports the entire feed inside a user-triggered retrieval job, so one embed miss can create dozens of topics and block the worker on network I/O

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item via `TopicEmbed.import`, which can create/update many topics/posts. Since `TopicRetriever` is invoked from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job enqueued on an embed miss in `EmbedController#best`, a single embed miss can cause the worker to block on network I/O and process the entire feed, potentially creating many topics as a side effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` has no open/read timeout and no size cap, so a slow or huge remote page hangs the Sidekiq worker and buffers the whole body in memory

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`. This uses open-uri to fetch the remote URL with no explicit open_timeout/read_timeout options and then calls `.read`, which buffers the entire response body into memory. As introduced here, a slow/unresponsive server can block the job/Sidekiq worker, and a very large response can cause excessive memory usage because the full body is read at once. No timeout or size limiting is present anywhere in this new code path in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:147 — replacing `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: ..., category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` drops the original creation date, so imported Disqus threads are dated 'now'; the `--category` option was removed and an unrescued fetch failure now aborts the whole import run

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the old code created the topic via `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)`, explicitly preserving the Disqus thread creation date and allowing an optional `--category`. The new code replaces that with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` ultimately calls `PostCreator.new(...)` without passing `created_at` or `category`, so the created topic/post will default to “now” and cannot be assigned to the selected category. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` with no rescue in the Thor task, so any network/HTTP/URI error will raise and abort the entire import run—this failure mode did not exist in the previous implementation which didn’t fetch remote content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:16,22 — the 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples don't stub `feed_polling_enabled?` (default false), so they pass even if the guards are deleted, and `poll_feed` itself (link/id fallback, nil content, import) has no coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` is only called when all three guards are true: `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the examples "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub `feed_polling_url` (nil) or `embed_by_username` (nil) respectively, but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Given the default in `config/site_settings.yml` is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, these specs can pass simply because the first guard is false, meaning they do not actually verify that the `feed_polling_url` / `embed_by_username` guards are necessary (they could be removed and the specs would still pass under the default setting). The additional note that `poll_feed` behavior has no direct coverage is also accurate from the diff (only `execute` is tested).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255), so longer URLs raise `StatementInvalid` on insert instead of being handled, and the unique index can't cover them

adjudication.rationale: In the new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`, `t.string :embed_url, null: false` creates a `varchar(255)` (default Rails string length) on typical DBs. The code stores arbitrary external URLs (`TopicEmbed.import` / `import_remote` using RSS links and `open(url)`), and there is no length validation/truncation logic—only presence validation. Therefore, an embed URL longer than 255 characters would cause an insert/update failure (e.g., `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` / value-too-long error) rather than being handled gracefully. The unique index itself isn’t the direct problem; the underlying 255-char column is what prevents longer URLs from being stored/indexed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` isn't atomic; a crash or Redis failover between the two leaves the key with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed URL; use `SET key 1 NX EX 60`

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterward gets a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes, is killed, or there is a Redis/network/failover issue between these two calls, the key can be left without an expiration, causing that embed URL to remain throttled indefinitely. Using a single atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` (or equivalent multi/transaction/Lua) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — the page reloads every 30s forever with no attempt counter, so an unretrievable URL causes an infinite reload loop hitting the server for every visitor

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the script unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` after 30000ms. The controller renders this `loading` view whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, and it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` each time. If the embed can’t be retrieved/created (e.g., remote fetch fails, parsing fails, missing embed_by_username/user, etc.), the page will keep reloading indefinitely, repeatedly hitting the server (and re-enqueuing the job) with no backoff or attempt limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — no `render_views`, so the broken `best.html.erb` template passes CI; success assertions also live in an `after` hook, where failures are reported against the wrong example
